A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same frozen-encoder multimodal alignment framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison across the changed title and organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original CKA simulations, projector and dataset ablations, and classification, retrieval, segmentation, multilingual, and dense-caption results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds encoder-unfreezing experiments, same-dataset CLIP comparisons, and multilingual segmentation results.

M1.justification: CKA-based encoder selection, concept-prototype data curation, residual token/CLS projectors, and contrastive training with frozen encoders remain unchanged. The newly evaluated unfreezing strategies are experimental alternatives, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds multilingual zero-shot segmentation using English, Spanish, Chinese, French, German, and Russian prompts (A.3). V1 already evaluated segmentation and multilingual classification/retrieval separately. The existing training sources and benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the direct controls: Table A.3 evaluates CLIP trained from scratch and CLIP with projector-only training on the authors' dataset, while Table A.2 compares projector training with BitFit and full text-encoder tuning. Existing CLIP, LiT, LiLT, SPARC, and multilingual comparators remain.

E3.justification: The reported real-embedding CKA experiment changes from 3,000 pairs with 35 text and 25 vision encoders to 5,000 pairs with five text and nine vision encoders (v1 Section 2.2; v2 Section 3.2). Additional mixture training changes from 30 to 15 epochs in the text. V2 also introduces 15-epoch unfreezing and 30-epoch CLIP comparisons; these reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New appendices A.1–A.2 directly test whether encoders should remain frozen and whether CLIP benefits similarly from the curated dataset. A.3 adds multilingual segmentation maps and language-sensitivity analysis. Existing projector, data-scaling, encoder-selection, and sDCI analyses are retained, while the real-embedding CKA-loss experiment is revised.

E5.justification: The Pearson correlations and p-values in v1 A.4 are retained in v2 A.7. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for the benchmark tables, and v2 introduces no new seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: All seven main tables and five pre-existing appendix tables retain their values. V2 adds substantial result sets for multilingual segmentation, unfreezing, and same-dataset CLIP training; Table A.3 newly reports ImageNet accuracies of 50.30%, 72.10%, and 76.45% for CLIP trained from scratch, CLIP projector training, and DINOv2-ARL. The revised real-embedding CKA plot retains the inverse relationship under changed settings.

T1.justification: The CKA/HSIC definitions and random-latent construction are retained, including material moved between the main text and appendix. V2 A.4 adds an unproved mathematical assertion that CLIP loss is lower-bounded by mutual information and uses its relationship with HSIC to argue about attainable alignment loss.

C1.justification: The central frozen-encoder framework and approximately 76% ImageNet claim remain. V2 explicitly qualifies the headline resource savings as alignment costs using pretrained encoders and describes dataset curation as supporting framework validation rather than establishing a distinct curation contribution.

C2.justification: V2 Section 6.5 explicitly assumes strong pretrained encoders are available and excludes their pretraining costs from the savings. Section 4.2 explains concept coverage through coverage of embedding spaces and reserves exhaustive curation for future work. The new controls also introduce interpretations concerning freezing tradeoffs and insufficient data for CLIP training from scratch.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a concrete code/curated-data repository address and reports encoder-pretraining resources. Most training details remain identical, including the 16k batch size, 30-epoch schedule, and eight-A100 setup. However, v1's explicit 128 images per concept prototype becomes unspecified few-shot sampling in v2.

R1.justification: V2 adds the MTEB citation and removes the two Dwivedi transfer-learning references, Eyes Wide Shut?, and the misplaced Radford 2019 language-model reference. The central positioning relative to CLIP, LiT, LiLT, and representational-similarity research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the introduction, framework motivation, and results narrative. Related work moves from Section 6 to Section 2, CKA definitions move into the main text, and the synthetic toy study and segmentation implementation move into the appendix.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint layout to two columns, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. V2 redraws the real-embedding CKA plot, rearranges existing embedding visualizations, and adds multilingual segmentation maps plus three tables. Several other displays are retained under new numbering or appendix placement.

improvement.justification: The new unfreezing and same-dataset CLIP controls strengthen evidence for important design choices that v1 did not directly test. The explicit pretraining-cost caveat and concrete resource link improve transparency. These gains are limited by briefly specified new protocols and the unreconciled 76.45% ImageNet result in Table A.3 versus 76.3% in the retained main Table 3.
